name: Badger
otherStatistics: AC 15 (+1 size, +3 Dex, +1 natural), touch 14, flat-footed 12. Base attack +0, grapple −5. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +4, Ref +5, Will +1.
appearance: A squat gray badger with black eye stripes, a pale face, broad shoulders and long digging claws.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersAnimals.rtf, Monsters (Animals) / Badger. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/badger.htm
sections.Full attack: Two claws, each +4 melee for 1d2−1, and one bite, −1 melee for 1d3−1.
sections.Special qualities:
Low-light vision. In dim illumination, see twice as far as a human with color and detail intact.
Scent (Ex). Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Double that range for strong odors and triple it for overpowering odors. A move action determines direction. Within 5 ft., locate the source exactly. Track and scent allow tracking by smell with a Wisdom or Survival check. A fresh trail typically starts at DC 10. Add 2 per hour the trail is cold and adjust for quarry count and odor. Surface conditions and poor visibility do not alter this scent check.
sections.Skills and feats: Escape Artist +7, Listen +3, Spot +3. Escape Artist includes a +4 racial bonus. Feats are Track (bonus) and Weapon Finesse.
sections.Encounter ecology: Temperate forests. Solitary, paired or a cete of 3–5. No treasure. Advances to 2 HD (Small). No level adjustment. Adults measure 2–3 ft. and weigh 25–35 lb.
sections.Special attacks and combat: Rage (Ex). After taking damage in combat, enter rage on the next turn and keep fighting until it or its opponent dies. Apply +4 Strength, +4 Constitution and −2 AC. It cannot end the rage voluntarily.

name: Dire Badger
otherStatistics: AC 16 (+3 Dex, +3 natural), touch 13, flat-footed 13. Base attack +2, grapple +4. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +7, Ref +6, Will +4.
appearance: An oversized, shaggy badger with a dark striped face, an arched back and enlarged digging claws.

sections.Special qualities:
Low-light vision. In dim illumination, see twice as far as a human with color and detail intact.
Scent (Ex). Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Double that range for strong odors and triple it for overpowering odors. A move action determines direction. name: Leopard
otherStatistics: AC 15 (+4 Dex, +1 natural), touch 14, flat-footed 11. Base attack +2, grapple +5. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +5, Ref +7, Will +2.
appearance: A long-tailed golden cat with dark rosettes, strong shoulders and a low stalking posture.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersAnimals.rtf, Monsters (Animals) / Leopard. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/leopard.htm
sections.Full attack: One bite, +6 melee for 1d6+3, and two claws, each +1 melee for 1d3+1.
sections.Special qualities:
Low-light vision. In dim illumination, see twice as far as a human with color and detail intact.
Scent (Ex). Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Double that range for strong odors and triple it for overpowering odors. A move action determines direction. Within 5 ft., locate the source exactly.
sections.Skills and feats: Balance +12, Climb +11, Hide +8, Jump +11, Listen +6, Move Silently +8, Spot +6. Racial bonuses are +8 Balance, Climb and Jump and +4 Hide and Move Silently. Tall grass or heavy undergrowth increases the racial Hide bonus to +8, for Hide +12. It can take 10 on Climb even when hurried or threatened. Feats are Alertness and Weapon Finesse.
sections.Encounter ecology: Warm forests. Solitary or paired. No treasure. Advances to 4–5 HD (Medium). No level adjustment. Usually hunts at night. The source also uses this block for comparably sized cats such as jaguars, panthers and mountain lions.
sections.Special attacks and combat:
Improved Grab (Ex). On a bite hit, attempt a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity or making a fresh touch attack. The generic rule limits this to a target at least one size smaller. A win pulls it into the leopard’s space and establishes a hold that allows rake attacks. A hold alone adds no damage. Each successful grapple check in subsequent rounds deals the bite damage. The leopard can hold using only its bite at −20 to its grapple checks, leaving itself free of the grapple while it holds the foe.
Pounce (Ex). Charge and make a full attack that includes two rake attacks.
Rake (Ex). +6 melee, 1d3+1. The general rake rule normally requires beginning the turn already grappling and removes the usual −4 penalty to natural attacks in a grapple. Pounce explicitly includes two rakes on its charge.

name: Pony
otherStatistics: AC 13 (+1 Dex, +2 natural), touch 11, flat-footed 12. Base attack +1, grapple +2. Space and reach 5 ft. each. Fort +4, Ref +4, Will +0.
appearance: A compact chestnut horse with sturdy short legs, a pale mane and a white facial blaze.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersAnimals.rtf, Monsters (Animals) / Pony. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/pony.htm
sections.Special qualities:
Low-light vision. In dim illumination, see twice as far as a human with color and detail intact.
Scent (Ex). Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Double that range for strong odors and triple it for overpowering odors. A move action determines direction. Within 5 ft., locate the source exactly.
sections.Encounter ecology: Temperate plains. Solitary. No treasure, advancement or level adjustment. Under 5 ft. at the shoulder. Carry 75 lb. as a light load, 76–150 lb. as a medium load, or 151–225 lb. as a heavy load. Drag up to 1,125 lb.
sections.Special attacks and combat: An ordinary pony cannot fight while carrying a rider. It generally flees rather than kicking. Its hoof is secondary and uses half its Strength bonus for damage, already factored into the table.
